sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Pettis County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Pettis County land are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Pettis County Courthouse, 415 South Ohio Ave, Suite 106, Sedalia, MO 65301. The main number is 660-826-5000 with extension 922, the fax is 660-829-4479, and the email address is recorder@pettiscomo.com. Barbara Clevenger is named on the county site as Recorder of Deeds.

The county page does not print counter hours, so call the extension before you drive in. Other courthouse offices post their own schedules; the collector, for one, is open 8:00 am to 5:00 pm on weekdays except holidays.

The office records deeds of trust, real estate deeds, releases, easements, subdivision plats, surveys, military discharges, powers of attorney, tax liens and real estate UCC filings. It also issues marriage licenses.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Pettis County?
sections.html:
The schedule posted on the county website lists $24 for the first page of a standard document and $3 for each page after it. That schedule predates the $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 that other Missouri recorders announce for August 28, 2026, so call 660-826-5000 ext 922 for what applies to your paper now.

A county policy lets the recorder keep an overpayment of up to $10, which cuts down on rejections for a check that is a dollar or two off. Anyone who wants an overpayment returned has to ask in writing within thirty days of the recording date, and the recorder then has thirty days to answer.

sections.h2: Can I search Pettis County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The recorder's page offers several routes, and each covers a different span of years:

  • Land records from 1983 to the present through the Fidlar Tapestry portal, which also holds marriage license and plat or survey searches back to 1833
  • A free online index book for land records research from 1833 through 1994, hosted at recordhub.cottsystems.com
  • Laredo, a monthly subscription that gives round the clock remote access to current data and images
  • Tapestry, a pay as you go service for people who search only now and then

Certified and plain copies of marriage licenses can be ordered through Official Records Online. Plan on checking the older index book first if a house has been in a family since before 1983, because the later database starts there.

sections.h2: What can the Pettis County recorder tell me about liens and sale prices?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ sets clear limits. Staff cannot search records by street address, so you need a legal description, a book and page, an owner name, the year of recording or a document number. The assessor's office in Suite 218 is where the county sends people who have only an address.

The same FAQ says the recorder is prohibited from running lien searches, because liens can also be filed with other offices. Staff will help you search the indexes yourself. A recorded deed does not have to state the sale price, so the office cannot tell you what a neighbor's house sold for. For easements, check the original plat and the indexes; there is no separate easement index.

Changing a name on a deed takes a new document, and the office does not prepare it. A title company or attorney does that work. After recording, expect the original back within about two weeks.

sections.h2: What format rules does the Pettis County recorder apply to deeds?
sections.html:
Pettis County follows the state layout statute, RSMo 59.310, which lets a recorder refuse a paper that falls short. The county fee schedule adds a $25 nonstandard charge for papers that are accepted despite format problems, and it points to the Recorders Association website for the formatting standards.

Under the statute, the paper must be printed on one side, in dark ink with type of at least eight point, on light colored stock of twenty pound weight or heavier. The top three inches of the first page are left open for the recorder's certificate, and signatures need a typed or printed name beneath them. Draft the deed with those points in mind, because a rejected paper means another trip or another mailing.

sections.h2: What is the Property Fraud Alert in Pettis County?
sections.html:
It is a free notification service the recorder offers to property owners, described on the county page as protection against property fraud, which happens when someone uses your property for financial gain. The recorder runs a similar sign up for notaries called Notary Fraud Alert. Both links sit on the recorder's page and run through Fidlar.

If you inherit a Pettis County house, or rent one out from a distance, setting up an alert costs nothing and sets up monitoring for the address.

sections.h2: Does the Pettis County recorder handle anything besides deeds?
sections.html:
Yes. Marriage licenses cost $60 including one certified copy on the posted schedule, with extra copies at $1 plain or $9 certified. Plain copies of recorded documents are $1 a page, and certifying a document is another $1. Survey pages are $24 for the first and $5 for each one after.

UCC fixture filings on the approved form with the required addendum are priced like a standard document, $24 for page one and $3 for each additional page. The office also records military discharges and tax liens.

sections.h2: What is Pettis County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Pettis County in west central Missouri was organized on January 24, 1833 and named for Spencer Darwin Pettis. Sedalia is both the seat and the largest city, and the county is home to the Missouri State Fair. It covers about 682 square miles of land. The 2020 census counted 42,980 people, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 44,254.

Other towns are Green Ridge, Houstonia, Hughesville, Ionia, La Monte, Smithton and Windsor. Public school districts with territory in the county include Sedalia 200, Pettis County R-V at Hughesville, Green Ridge R-VIII, La Monte R-IV and Smithton.

sections.h2: Which Pettis County offices should I call before a sale?
sections.html:
The assessor, collector and recorder all sit in the courthouse at 415 S Ohio, which keeps a title check to one stop.

  • Assessor Christopher Woolery, Suite 218, ext 920, for the parcel's classification and value
  • Collector Marsha Boeschen, Suite 216, ext 921, for tax statements and receipts; online payments run through a Devnet portal with a card fee of at least $1.55 or 2.45 percent, and e-checks carry no fee
  • Recorder, Suite 106, ext 922, for recorded deeds and releases

Ask the collector for the current year's balance before closing day. The collector says a paid receipt can take a week to ten days to appear after an online payment, and an e-check about ten days to clear.

faqs.q: Is the Pettis County recorder fee schedule current?
faqs.a: The posted schedule shows $24 for page one, which was set before the $2.00 statewide increase Missouri recorders announced for August 28, 2026. Call 660-826-5000 ext 922 for the amount charged today.

faqs.q: Can Pettis County staff find a deed if I only know the street address?
faqs.a: No. The recorder cannot search by street address and needs a legal description, a book and page, a name, the recording year or a document number. The assessor's office can supply the legal description from the address.

faqs.q: How long until I get my original deed back from the Pettis County recorder?
faqs.a: The county FAQ says you should receive the original within two weeks of recording.

faqs.q: Does a Pettis County deed show the sale price?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The county states that the selling price is not required on a recorded deed, so the recorder cannot report what a nearby home sold for.

faqs.q: What if I overpay the recording fee in Pettis County?
faqs.a: The recorder keeps overpayments of up to $10 under county policy. To get a refund, send a written request within thirty days of the recording date.
